transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, nice to meet you too. I guess what brings me in is... I just can't keep my mind on one thing anymore. Like, I work at this warehouse, right? And lately, every little thing pulls my attention away. A beeper goes off, or the forklift alarm starts backing up—beep, beep, beep—you know that sound? My neighbor actually bought a truck that makes that exact noise when he backs into his driveway, which is just ridiculous because it's a residential street, not a loading dock. Anyway, someone moves a pallet, and boom, I'm completely off my count. Then I look down and realize I've put all the wrong numbers into the inventory system. Which reminds me, they updated the software last week, and the new interface is just terrible. The buttons are so small... but yeah, I just can't stay focused.
Did you have trouble paying attention as a child?

I don't think so, no. I don't remember having any issues like that when I was a kid. I actually did pretty well in school, at least back then. I remember my fourth-grade teacher, Mr. Henderson, he used to give out these little gold star stickers if you paid attention and finished your reading early. I had a whole notebook covered in them. It was one of those Trapper Keepers, you know the ones? With the velcro flap? I loved that thing. My daughter bought her son a binder for school this year and it just feels so cheap, like the plastic is going to crack in a week. They really don't make things like they used to. Even the pallets at the warehouse—half the time the wood is already splintered before we even load anything onto them, which just makes a huge mess on the floor...
Have there been times lately when you felt unusually energized and needed much less sleep than usual?

Unusually energized? No, I don't think so. I mean, I sleep my regular hours, mostly. Though honestly, my mattress has been giving me a terrible backache lately. It's one of those memory foam ones, and I swear it just traps all the heat. I wake up sweating half the time. 

My sister keeps telling me I need to buy one of those cooling mattress pads, the ones they always advertise on those late-night infomercials. I used to watch those all the time when I was working the night shift back in the late nineties. They always had that one guy with the really loud voice selling stain remover or whatever. He always seemed so energized, just yelling at the camera about getting red wine out of a white carpet. I always wondered who is spilling that much wine at three in the morning anyway? And why white carpet? It just seems like you're asking for trouble if you have kids or pets. My golden retriever used to track mud in all the time... 

But yeah, no, my sleep is pretty much the same as always. I haven't noticed needing less of it or anything.
Did these focus problems start after something stressful happened in your life?

Stressful? Well, let me think... I don't really know if it was one specific thing. I mean, work is always a little stressful, right? Especially when they do those inventory audits. They bring in these outside consultants who walk around with their little clipboards, judging how we stack the boxes. One of them last month had this incredibly loud sneeze—like, startled the whole warehouse loud. It reminded me of my uncle Arthur. He used to sneeze so hard he'd throw his back out. He was a mechanic, always bent over cars, so his back was already bad. He worked on this beautiful vintage Mustang once, cherry red. I always wanted a red car, but my husband—well, ex-husband now—insisted on silver because he said it didn't show the dirt as much. Which is a total lie, by the way, silver shows every speck of road salt in the winter. We used to drive up to the mountains every winter, back when my knees could handle skiing... but to answer your question, no, I can't really pinpoint any big stressful event that started all this. It just sort of... happened.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot, even about everyday things?

Worrying? No, not really. I mean, I don't think I worry any more than the next person. Just the usual stuff, you know? Paying the bills, making sure the car passes inspection... Oh, speaking of inspections, I took my Honda in last week and the guy told me I needed all new brake pads. I swear they always try to upsell you on something when you go in for a simple oil change. It's like that time I went to buy a new washing machine at Sears—well, back when Sears was still open at the mall. The salesman kept trying to get me to buy this extended warranty that cost almost as much as the machine itself. I told him, "Look, buddy, I just need something that gets the grease out of my work shirts." Working at the warehouse, you get this weird black dust on everything, it just clings to the fabric. I've tried every detergent in the aisle, even that expensive eco-friendly stuff my daughter swears by. She's all into natural products now, makes her own deodorant and everything. Smells a bit like pine needles, if I'm being honest. But anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, worrying. Yeah, no, I don't think I'm a big worrier. Just regular everyday stuff.
